Am in Brisbane.Was recommended to Solar Secure by a colleague at work who had a few other friends settle on this company to install their solar systems. They are certainly one of the most competitively priced companies around selling lower end/reputable Chinese products (18x Trina Solar Honey 370W panels & Growatt 5kW inverter with wifi stick for $3150 on a 2 story house). They also did not have a product to monitor solar energy consumption (the wifi module tells you how much production you have and the inverter will switch off at night). There are newer Trina 390/400W panels as well offered by other companies... something to keep in mind.My main hesitation was Solar Secure hadn't been registered for long (~ 2 years) and not sure how warranty issues would go if something were to happen over the next few years if they disappeared. They will negotiate on price if you get a similar/better deal from another company.I did find the sales process to be pretty annoying frankly. They don't need to be so pushy as it could definitely turn off a few people - I was almost one of those. Lots of sales speak with not enough useful information for the customer. Also watch out for the reviews they keep pushing you to read as there are also unhappy customers on other review platforms.I had to advocate for the best inverter placement (inside my garage) and placement of a split array of panels due to ventilation shafts on my NW roof. They were not very informative as other companies in doing an analysis of where the best placement of panels is to maximise energy production. Between other websites (Solar Quotes, Solcast & SunEarthTools) I was able to work out the placement that would fit in with our usage of high drain electricity devices Vs time of day across the different seasons. (mainly pool pump, cooking, washing, heating/cooling during daytime).They did point out my switchboard needing an upgrade and gave me a rough price, but ended up getting my own electrician do that work before the PV system install.The install was done about 2-3 weeks after paying the deposit/doing paperwork. They subcontract to 2 installers who were pretty efficient and clean. Just one mistake which they rectified (dropped a bracket on to my tin deck roof and punctured a hole). The installer was very apologetic and patched it as best as he could. If it was a still a problem he would be happy to get a proper roofing company to replace the sheet of roofing.Solar Secure were quick with all the paperwork and my electricity retailer had the meter mode swapped remotely in the next day or so after install.Overall they are very economical, quick and the installers were good. Sales process was painful though... he probably just needs to cut the words in half and allow customers to consider their options, without any pressure tactics. As a customer you will need to do some research to find out what is best for your electricity usage & panel/inverter placement... they were pretty lacking in this department.Also get everything in writing before paying. Read their PDS/terms & conditions... if you are concerned about roof damage their terms are not as generous as other companies. There is a cooling off period of 10 business days (not 10 calendar days as the sales person thought) just in case you get cold feet.
